stem:
A research satellite moves in a circular orbit 400 km above the surface of the Earth.

Mass of the Earth $= 6.0 \times 10^{24}$ kg  ·  Radius of the Earth $= 6.4 \times 10^{6}$ m

parts.label: a
parts.question: Show that the orbital speed of the satellite is about $7.7 \times 10^{3}$ m s$^{-1}$.
markscheme: $v = \sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{r}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 6.0 \times 10^{24}}{6.8 \times 10^{6}}}$ $= 7.67 \times 10^{3}$ m s$^{-1}$ (answer must be given to at least 3 s.f. for a 'show that') ✓

parts.label: b
parts.question: Calculate the orbital period of the satellite in minutes.

parts.label: c
parts.question: An astronaut inside the satellite says she feels 'weightless'. Explain, with reference to the forces acting, why this happens even though the gravitational field strength at this height is about 90% of its value at the surface.
markscheme: The astronaut and the satellite are both in free fall, with the same acceleration towards the Earth (gravity provides the centripetal force) ✓
So there is no contact/normal force between the astronaut and the floor, and this contact force is what we sense as weight ✓
